reviews.evidence: Ships LAN and optional remote mobile access, persistent pairing, Android/browser paths, device controls, and /mobile customization; the README gives complete connection flows, prompt-to-UI examples, screenshots, compatibility gates, security controls, cleanup, and verification commands.
reviews.concern: Remote access inherits third-party bandwidth/platform limits, and host extensions run with the local user's privileges; examples are rich but not full case studies with measured outcomes.

reviews.evidence: Provides relay- and project-attributed usage, balances and subscription windows, cost estimation, analysis, export, diagnostics, reindexing, custom endpoints, API/library access, and detailed commands; correctness edge cases, tests, security boundaries, and recovery behavior are explicit.
reviews.concern: Only one panel screenshot is a concrete visual demonstration, and the explicit scenarios are mainly troubleshooting, unsupported-provider declaration, and project-cost attribution rather than detailed case studies.

reviews.evidence: Ships exact multi-frame previews, an interactive canvas, managed editing, direct-canvas tools, and a transactional draft-to-publish pipeline with detailed operational sequencing; it documents gates, rollback, recovery drafts, conflicts, six-platform packaging, tests, fallbacks, and current limits.
reviews.concern: The README has only one main product screenshot, while most output evidence is descriptive; explicit when-to-use guidance covers production, one-shot, and existing-canvas work but not worked user case studies.

reviews.evidence: Covers runtime injection, reload/self-reload, watch, UI linkage, staging and promotion, uninstall, route repair, restart recovery, scaffolding, build, release, and self-test; it gives install alternatives, production workflows, a daemon example, stress-test claims, rollback behavior, and concrete failure lessons.
reviews.concern: Demonstration evidence is primarily commands, code, and reported test results rather than captured end-user outputs, and several performance-guidance sections extend beyond the injector's central workflow.

reviews.evidence: Its own marketplace workflow spans indexed discovery, search/filtering, type detection, guarded installation, materials handoff, installed-state recognition, updates, uninstall, backup/restore, feedback, and diagnostics; GUI steps, endpoint result states, security controls, fallbacks, and limitations are extensively documented.
reviews.concern: The visible hero is decorative rather than a product-state demo, and reliability evidence is broad but lacks an in-README reproducible test run or concrete test-result summary sufficient for the exceptional anchor.

reviews.evidence: Ships a Galgame-styled desktop agent with animated characters, voice/BGM, nine provider presets, setup wizard, persona editing, uploads, quick commands, save slots, and updating; multiple screenshots show chat, configuration, character editing, and settings states.
reviews.concern: Most instructions are installation or configuration, with only a partial '/' interaction beyond setup; the README gives one brief fan/immersive-use persona and only limited compatibility, limits, and connection-validation evidence.

reviews.evidence: Ships a varied set of completed infrastructure and visualization skills, with explicit prompts and expected outputs for kernel development, memory estimation, RL setup, flowcharts, and slides, plus several linked or embedded generated artifacts and pytest commands.
reviews.concern: The project explicitly warns that content is heavily LLM-generated without strict proofreading; quality standards and validation are stated, but the README does not show executed test results for the full collection.

reviews.evidence: Ships a desktop Harness with launcher, Git actions, file/diff/browser/agent surfaces, terminal, model controls, appearance, extension management, tray/update, restart, and plugin recovery; shortcuts, migration recovery, screenshots, compatibility requirements, tests, checksums, and production acceptance gates are explicit.
reviews.concern: Operational guidance for everyday Git, terminal, and extension tasks is mostly feature-level or shortcut-level rather than complete workflows, while explicit scenarios concentrate on startup, upgrade migration, and crash recovery.

reviews.evidence: Provides an end-to-end macOS flow for permission handling, action recording, session inspection, recording validation, evidence packaging, and agent skill handoff; the README includes a worked file-sending demo, several other explicit UI scenarios, CLI reference, and concrete artifact trees.
reviews.concern: It is explicitly alpha and macOS-only, screenshots are outside the core recording path, and demonstrations show artifact structures rather than a completed learned skill or multiple measured outcomes.

reviews.evidence: Ships previewable five-part session handoff, clean-target creation, optional continuation, editable native cards, image policies, client fallbacks, and a contract doctor; commands, a real migration GIF, quantified release gates, fail-closed behavior, compatibility matrix, limits, and a 160-test package gate are documented.
reviews.concern: The central explicit use case is switching presets mid-task with a few image/client variants, and the README itself cautions that timing and native-card samples are small release evidence rather than population guarantees.
